subject: Orion Health renewal — support layer bump & latency SLOs
messages:
From: Amelia Soto <amelia@orionhealth.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@orionhealth.ai
Date: Fri, 12 Sep 2025 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal discussion — capacity and SLA needs

Hi Rishi / Marissa,

Our current agreement is up at the end of October. Over the past 12 months we’ve leaned heavily on Redwood for real-time clinical triage in our platform and we’re seeing traffic spikes during influenza season that breached our current bursts. For the renewal we need two things: a committed capacity uplift (roughly +40% sustained for Q4) and a formalized Premium SLA that includes a 99.5% p95 latency SLO for inference requests under 2s.

Procurement is looped in (procurement@orionhealth.ai) and will need a commercial proposal and the new SLA language to run internally. Can we set a time early next week to review proposed changes and the cost delta? I’ve attached a quick workbook with our projected token volumes.

Thanks,
Amelia Soto
Director, Platform Integrations
Orion Health

Attachments: Orion_Capacity_Workbook_Q3-Q4-2025.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 12 Sep 2025 14:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — capacity and SLA needs

Hi Amelia — thanks for the context and the workbook. We can absolutely support a committed uplift and formalize a Premium SLA to cover latency targets. High-level thoughts: 

- We can propose a 12‑month renewal with a 40% committed capacity uplift and automated burst buffer for seasonal spikes.
- Premium SLA can include: 99.5% p95 latency under a 2s target for standard inference requests running on the dedicated pool, monthly performance credits for breach windows, and a named escalation path with 4-hour P1 response.
- Commercial delta: I’ll run a preliminary estimate against your workbook and include a couple of options (12‑month vs 24‑month term, and an optional 2-week onboarding + throughput tuning engagement).

I’m attaching our draft SLA proposal and a pricing worksheet — Marissa, can you add an Ops onboarding estimate and proposed timeline? Ben, we’ll need you to validate latency feasibility for their model mix (long-context clinical prompts). Vivek — flagging for visibility since this is a strategic upsell for the healthcare vertical.

Proposed times: Mon 9/15 11:00am PT or Tue 9/16 9:00am PT for a 30-min sync. Which works for you?

– Rishi
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0179

Thanks Rishi — Tue 9/16 9:00am PT works for us.

A couple of clarifying asks ahead of the call so we can prepare on our side:
- Will the Premium SLA require us to move to a Dedicated pool, or can Redwood guarantee the SLO on our current shared-hosted setup?
- For monthly performance credits: can you outline the calculation (tokens, minutes of breach, or percentage of invoices)?

Procurement will want to see sample SLA language and a clear playbook for how Redwood handles incidents with clinical impact. Ethan will join the call to cover procurement / risk items.

Regards,
Amelia

Hi Amelia — quick note before tomorrow’s call from the infra/SE side. Short answers:

- Dedicated pool recommended for deterministic p95 latency at scale. We can run a QoS test on your workload against a dedicated pool during onboarding (1–2 day light test).
- Credits: standard practice is invoice-based credits tied to SLO breach windows; we calculate credits as a percentage of monthly recurring fees proportionate to minutes of breached SLO in the month (example language in the attached proposal).
- For long-context clinical prompts we’ll want to test sequence-length distributions — that’s the biggest driver of latency variance. If you can share 48–72 hours of anonymized request traces, we’ll run a tuning pass.

I’ve merged a short ops timeline into the attached proposal (RDW_Premium_SLA_Proposal_2025-09-12.pdf). Looking forward to the call.

— Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Thanks everyone for a productive call this morning. Recap and agreed next steps below — please reply if anything is missing or incorrect.

Recap (agreed):
- Term: 12 months starting 2025-11-01.
- Capacity: +40% committed throughput (Q4 uplift) with a 15% automated burst buffer for seasonal volatility.
- Deployment: Customer will move to a Dedicated pool (RDW-ded-OR-01) to meet the 99.5% p95 < 2s latency SLO.
- SLA: Monthly performance credits for breach (credit % scale in attached proposal), 4-hour named P1 response, and a joint incident runbook for clinically sensitive outages.
- Onboarding: 2-week Ops tuning engagement (ben to run QoS tests and tuning). Tentative start: 2025-11-02.
- Commercial: Amelia — procurement asked for a single-line quote for the committed capacity + Premium SLA, plus an optional 2-week onboarding fee. I will push a formal quote and DocuSign envelope by EOD 9/16.

Action items:
- Rishi: Send final SLA PDF and single-line commercial quote (by EOD today).
- Ben: Share QoS test checklist and request for anonymized 72-hour traces.
- Marissa: Draft onboarding timeline and internal CS kickoff calendar invite.
- Amelia / Procurement: Confirm billing entity and PO timing.
